item.title: StateBench benchmark evaluates long‑context state tracking in language models
item.description:
StateBench benchmark evaluates long‑context state tracking in language models

A new benchmark called StateBench has been introduced to measure how well language models keep track of information about entities in long documents as those entities evolve.

🔍 Overview

  • State tracking is needed for tasks such as reading code (variables are assigned and reassigned) and following a story where characters move and objects change hands.
  • Example: a mystery novel states “John gave Mary the knife” right before a murder; the model must know that the state of each character has changed.
  • Some state‑tracking problems only require finding the latest update; harder ones require following a chain of changes where missing a single step can alter the final answer.

🧩 How it works

StateBench captures state‑tracking problems of four increasing difficulty levels:

Difficulty level Update type Concrete example
R‑trivial Immutable assignment – a variable’s value never changes. Code: let x = 4; Everyday: a birth date that stays fixed.
Aperiodic Reassignment by value – the model only needs the most recent value. Code: x = 4 later x = 2; Everyday: a thermostat where the latest setting determines temperature.
Soluble Self‑referential updates – each update builds on the current value. Code: x = x + 5; Everyday: a game score where each point adds to the running total.
General finite Assignment by reference – one variable can take another variable’s current value, creating cross‑update dependencies. Code: x = y or swapping two variables; Everyday: a magician swapping a ball under five cups (the S₅ state‑tracking problem).

⚙️ Evaluation

  • Researchers tested a range of open pretrained models on the r‑trivial, aperiodic, and general finite levels of StateBench.
  • Findings:
    • Recurrent and hybrid models (e.g., Gated DeltaNet) can generalize much farther than transformers when trained directly on these tasks.
    • Frontier models—including Gemini 3.8 Flash, Claude Opus 5.5, and GPT‑6 Sol and Luna—still break down on harder forms of state tracking as inputs grow longer.
  • Theoretical expectations:
    • Under standard assumptions, transformers handle r‑trivial robustly and can manage soluble and aperiodic to some degree, but are predicted to fail on general problems.
    • Gated DeltaNet, with a flexible memory update, can in principle handle all four levels.

💡 Why it matters

  • Accurate state tracking underlies practical applications such as code analysis and narrative comprehension.
  • Existing tests focus on the hardest cases, but as recurrent and hybrid designs become more common, researchers need benchmarks that reveal which kinds of state tracking each architecture can handle.
  • StateBench provides this granularity, helping the community assess and improve long‑context reasoning capabilities across model families.

#StateBench #LongContext #AIbenchmarks

Source: StateBench: Testing how language models track state changes over long documents

item.title: PremiseCheck: LLM rewriting plus a decision model for review comments
item.description:
PremiseCheck: LLM rewriting plus a decision model for review comments

A new cross-disciplinary approach to evaluating factuality in review comments has been introduced. ReviewFact labels factual errors across NLP, machine learning, and the natural sciences, and it measures cost and latency alongside accuracy. PremiseCheck combines this approach into a framework that uses an LLM to rewrite comments into explicit premises and a decision model to verify them against the paper.

🔍 Overview

  • “ReviewFact labels factual errors across NLP, machine learning, and the natural sciences, and that measures cost and latency alongside accuracy.”
  • “PremiseCheck is a framework that combines the two.”
  • “An LLM rewrites each comment as explicit premises without reading the paper, and a decision model checks each premise against the paper.”
  • “When each comment is checked on its own, PremiseCheck reaches accuracy comparable to GPT-5.5 across all three fields at about half its cost, and on NLP reviews at a quarter of its cost and less than half its latency.”
  • “A frontier LLM checks comments well but must read the whole paper for each check, while cheap decision models, which score whether a statement holds in a text, fall far short on whole comments that mix several implicit assertions.”

🧩 How it works

  • “PremiseCheck is a framework that combines the two.”
  • “An LLM rewrites each comment as explicit premises without reading the paper, and a decision model checks each premise against the paper.”
  • “A frontier LLM checks comments well but must read the whole paper for each check, while cheap decision models, which score whether a statement holds in a text, fall far short on whole comments that mix several implicit assertions.”

⚙️ Key details

  • When each comment is checked on its own, PremiseCheck reaches accuracy comparable to GPT-5.5 across all three fields at about half its cost, and on NLP reviews at a quarter of its cost and less than half its latency.

💡 Why it matters

  • ReviewFact provides a cross-disciplinary benchmark for labeling factual errors in review comments and for measuring cost and latency alongside accuracy.
  • PremiseCheck demonstrates how combining an LLM-based rewrite step with a decision-model check can pair strong accuracy with improved efficiency across NLP, ML, and the natural sciences.

#ReviewFact #PremiseCheck #Factuality #CrossDiscipline #ArtificialIntelligence

Source: PremiseCheck: Efficient Fact-Checking of Human and AI Peer Reviews

item.title: LLM Leaderboard 2026 Update Ranks Over 300 AI Models
item.description:
LLM Leaderboard 2026 Update Ranks Over 300 AI Models

The LLM Leaderboard has updated its rankings for 2026, evaluating and comparing more than 300 AI models. The ranking aggregates performance across intelligence, output speed, latency, and per-token pricing into a single metric called the LLM Stats Score, utilizing continuous updates from provider APIs and verified benchmarks.

📊 Benchmark Highlights

Recent evaluations highlight top-performing models across major benchmark categories including reasoning, coding, speed, and context size:

Category Model Metric Details

Cheapest Input Mistral NeMo Instruct $0.02 / 1M tok
Largest Context Grok-4.1 Fast Non-Reasoning 2M tokens Biggest context window

🔓 Open-Weight Model Rankings

The leaderboard also maintains an independent ranking of open-weight large language models—including Llama, Qwen, GLM, DeepSeek, Mistral, Kimi, and others—evaluated by coding-arena score, GPQA Diamond, throughput, latency, and per-token pricing:

  • Best Open-Weight / Best on GPQA Diamond: Kimi K3 (93.5% GPQA)
  • Best for Coding (Arena): DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 (24.1 arena score)
  • Best on AIME 2025: Kimi K2-Thinking-0905 (100.0%)
  • Best on SWE-Bench Verified: DeepSeek-V4-Pro-Max (80.6%)
  • Highest Throughput: Mistral Small 4 (73 tok/s)
  • Lowest Latency: Mistral Small 4 (1413.90 s)
  • Cheapest Input: Mistral NeMo Instruct ($0.02 / 1M tok)
  • Largest Context Window: Kimi K3 (1.0M tokens)
